definition: Changing one thing and re-running to see what the output would have been, and across 3 sources the design that separates the archive's grounded causal claims from its correlational ones. Its instances: masking the evidence a system cites and finding 82.8 percent of correct answers flip while masking uncited evidence changes 9.6; re-running a reasoning trace from a modified prefix to locate the sentences that commit a model to agreeing with an incorrect user suggestion; and intervening on cross-attention in a diffusion model to test what a component contributes. The archive's related finding, from the trace literature, is what makes this design necessary: reasoning traces shape outputs while models will not say so, so a self-report is not a substitute for a counterfactual and a correlation between a trace feature and an answer establishes neither direction.

evidence.note: Recasts long-document visual question answering as building an explicit evidence graph whose nodes are grounded document blocks and whose edges are reasoning dependencies, and verifies the graph causally — masking the evidence it cites flips 82.8% of correct answers while masking uncited evidence changes 9.6%.
evidence.title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning

evidence.note: Injects synthetic reasoning into a model's trace, shows the injection changes the answer, then shows the model refuses to admit it and fabricates an unrelated explanation instead.
evidence.title: Reasoning Traces Shape Outputs but Models Won't Say So

evidence.note: Traces how individual prompt tokens ground into image regions during diffusion denoising, using fixed-seed single-word removal for causal faithfulness and a head-resolved spike score for attribution.
evidence.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Cross-Attention Interventions

name: counterfactual intervention
